notes: Batch AE (progestogens, vaginal estriol/lactobacillus, oral corticosteroids): progesterone, norethisterone, dydrogesterone, estriol-lactobacillus, prednisolone, dexamethasone. NO-UK-PRODUCT: estriol-lactobacillus (vaginal tablet combining estriol with Lactobacillus acidophilus): emc search by trade name, estriol and lactobacillus, and the MHRA Products search index (queried through the public search endpoint the products.mhra.gov.uk page itself uses) by trade name, lactobacillus and estriol found only estriol-only products. DIFFERENT UK STRENGTHS USED: norethisterone clinic 10 mg tablets -> UK 5 mg tablet SmPCs (no UK 10 mg tablet found); prednisolone clinic syrup 15 mg/5 mL -> UK 10 mg/mL oral solution SmPC (no UK 3 mg/mL product found); dexamethasone clinic 0.5 mg/5 mL syrup -> UK 2 mg/5 mL oral solution SmPCs (no UK 0.5 mg/5 mL found). Each flagged in formulations[].note. Prednisolone 20 mg tablets: UK SPC exists only on MHRA Products (PL 00142/0844), used as mhra-pl00142-0844-spc. CONFLICTS / DIFFERENCES BETWEEN UK SOURCES: (1) Norethisterone: the originator 5 mg SmPC (emc-1135, updated 2019) lists lactation, high thrombosis risk, migraine with focal symptoms, diabetes with vascular involvement, liver tumours, sex-hormone-dependent malignancy and untreated endometrial hyperplasia as contraindications; the generic 5 mg SmPC (emc-1494) does not, but lists disturbance of liver function and porphyria and licenses high-dose use for disseminated breast carcinoma (so the sex-hormone-dependent tumour contraindication from emc-1135 conflicts with the generic breast-carcinoma indication; both shown in the rule). Breastfeeding rule is contraindicated per emc-1135 (generic SmPC silent). Period-delay duration: emc-1135 says no longer than 10-14 days, SPS says up to 3-4 weeks if necessary; both shown. (2) Prednisolone contraindications differ by UK product: 5 mg tablet (emc-14313) systemic infection without anti-infective cover + ocular herpes simplex; 10 mg/mL solution (emc-101838) systemic infection + live virus immunisation; 20 mg tablet (MHRA) systemic fungal infection + live vaccines at immunosuppressive doses. Rules are formulation-scoped accordingly; interaction rules are molecule-level. (3) Dexamethasone breastfeeding: emc-11015 says breastfeeding is discouraged (avoid), emc-1344 says weigh benefits, SPS says use with caution (alternatives preferred) - two separate rules kept. Dexamethasone pregnancy: SmPCs say not for maternal indications unless clearly necessary (avoid), BUMPS says systemic corticosteroids can be used if recommended by a doctor; rule keeps SmPC strength and quotes BUMPS in action. Dexamethasone contraindications differ: emc-11015 adds acute viral infection and live vaccination; emc-1344 adds systemic infection without anti-infective cover and says contraindications generally do not apply when life-saving. (4) Prednisolone pregnancy: SmPC benefit/risk (caution) vs BUMPS usually among safest options. GROUPS: progestogen members (progesterone, norethisterone, dydrogesterone) and corticosteroid members (prednisolone, dexamethasone) sourced from their own SmPC 5.1. Added metformin to group antidiabetic (quoting emc-987 from batch D, 5.1 Blood glucose lowering drugs) because the oral steroid SmPCs name insulin, sulfonylureas and metformin / hypoglycaemic agents and metformin alone was not yet an antidiabetic member. GROUP MAPPING CAVEATS: corticosteroid CYP3A inhibitor rules use group:cyp3a4-inhibitor (SmPC wording is CYP3A inhibitors incl. cobicistat). Enzyme-inducer rules use group:cyp3a4-inducer for progestogens (norethisterone and dydrogesterone SmPCs say inducers of CYP enzymes generally). Norethisterone rules rely on other batches sourcing members of group:tetracycline (SmPC: tetracyclines) and group:azole-antifungal (SmPC example: fluconazole); members are sourced in batch AA (doxycycline) and AC (fluconazole, miconazole); the azole rule is info-level and the SmPC example is fluconazole, so it will also show for miconazole products. Steroid interactions with NSAIDs, salicylates and anticoagulants carry effect bleeding; methotrexate carries bone-marrow-suppression. Live vaccines are not in the master list, so the live-vaccine 4.3 items are condition rules (new condition live-vaccine). Progesterone SmPC says concomitant vaginal products are not recommended: encoded only against estriol-lactobacillus (the only all-vaginal master-list product known to this batch); vaginal forms of clotrimazole, miconazole or fenticonazole should get the same rule if the integrator can scope by their vaginal formulation ids. NOT FOUND / NOT VERIFIED: no BUMPS leaflet for progesterone, norethisterone or dydrogesterone (404); no SPS breastfeeding page for the progestogens; no UK renal advice for dydrogesterone; norethisterone and dexamethasone/prednisolone 4.8 give no frequencies except psychiatric reactions (common). MHRA DSU searched (corticosteroids, progestogens, norethisterone, dydrogesterone, meningioma): nothing product-specific beyond what the SmPCs already state, so not cited. No UK source states brand-name prescribing for any medicine in this batch. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/AD-AE.md): DYDROGESTERONE kept as a UK product: the source is Nalvee 10 mg film-coated tablets (PL 04854/0198, first authorised 21/06/2024, text revised 07/08/2026), a current UK licence; the old Duphaston licence is not used (MHRA products also lists Dydrogesterone Waymade 10 mg, PL 06464/3141). ESTRIOL-LACTOBACILLUS no-uk-product confirmed: emc 'No search results' for the trade name and for lactobacillus; MHRA products index 0 hits for the trade name, and every estriol hit has substance ESTRIOL only. Progesterone 'concomitant vaginal products not recommended' now also encoded against the vaginal formulation ids of clotrimazole, miconazole, fenticonazole and clindamycin (otherFormulations), and all five rules say 'when progesterone is given vaginally'. Progesterone adverseCommon corrected from the HTML 4.8 tables (altered mood is uncommon in ART). Norethisterone: formulation note clarified (UK '1 tablet' = 5 mg, not one clinic 10 mg tablet); macrolide group rule narrowed to clarithromycin (the SmPC lists macrolides as CYP3A4 inhibitors, azithromycin is not named); new emc-1135 4.4 rules for depression, diabetes and lactose; breast-tumour action wording fixed. Dydrogesterone: new monitor rule for cholestatic jaundice/pruritus. Prednisolone and dexamethasone syrup notes now give the mL conversion and say UK excipient warnings may not apply to the clinic syrups.
